editorial.brief: All five of Wikipedia's most-read pages are election-related, led by Abdul El-Sayed at 1,413,749 views, and Lemmy, Bluesky, Mastodon and Polymarket are counting the same votes. Hacker News looked elsewhere, giving 881 points to residential proxies on the White House network. Heat vs. Clippers turned up in both search and betting.
editorial.cover_sub: Abdul El-Sayed drew 1,413,749 views, ahead of two other candidates and the elections page itself, on a day when Lemmy, Bluesky, Mastodon and Polymarket were all counting votes.
editorial.wiki_deck: Abdul El-Sayed led Wikipedia with 1,413,749 views, a thin margin over James Talarico. The entire top five belongs to the 2026 elections.
editorial.letter_headline: A day spent reading the election returns
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is suspicious of White House networks, giving 881 points to residential proxies. Lemmy is celebrating election night, Bluesky is tired and sentimental, and Mastodon is proud of newly elected scientists.
editorial.foreign_deck: With no wire stories in the snapshot, the searches speak: afg vs zim in Britain, India and the US, Powerball in Britain and the US, and typhoon information in Japan.
editorial.markets_deck: Three of five are Senate races at 95 to 96 percent. Heat vs. Clippers sits at 28 percent and aliens confirmed before 2027 at 2 percent, both on $2 million.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,268,241 players, ahead of PUBG at 811,300, Dota 2 at 717,007 and Phantom Blade Zero at 687,823. On Twitch, caseoh_ led with 58,283 viewers.
editorial.yt_headline: A Worlds quarterfinal, GEN vs LYON
editorial.yt_note: Esports leads at 1,496,141 views. The rest is music and trailers: Kevin Gates at 213,396, an Angry Birds Movie 3 trailer at 183,251, and a Lords of War teaser at 315,054.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow the Talarico and Hinojosa pages will likely be quieter, and Heat vs. Clippers will have a result. The 95 percent Peltola market will resolve or drift. The White House proxy story may gain a sequel. Bluesky will have moved on from Robert Palmer.
wiki_paras: Abdul El-Sayed was the most-read article on Wikipedia, with 1,413,749 views. James Talarico followed at 1,256,040 and Gina Hinojosa at 1,242,354. The 2026 United States elections page took fourth with 1,153,444, and Jon Ossoff completed the five at 611,863. Nothing unrelated to the election made the list.

The margin was thin. El-Sayed led second place by about 158,000 views, a ratio of 1.1 to one. The top four sit within roughly 260,000 views of each other, a pack rather than a runaway, and then Ossoff falls away to less than half the leader's total.

The rest of the data supplies the explanation. Lemmy's top posts concern election night, including a headline about Democrats in Texas and a Montana ballot initiative. Bluesky carries a Talarico quote, Mastodon lists newly elected scientists, and Polymarket prices Senate races at 95 and 96 percent. The snapshot does not say what office El-Sayed sought.
letter_paras: This was a single-story day. Wikipedia's top five are all election pages or candidates, Lemmy's front page is mostly election night, and Polymarket's busiest contracts include Senate races priced at 95 and 96 percent. Hacker News and Steam kept their own counsel, but the center of gravity was plain. Twenty-five earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or above barely registered against it.

Some smaller entries. A Bluesky post credits Mary Sherman Morgan as America's first female rocket scientist. GitHub trending offers a Rust tool called worktrunk and a Shell repository called skills. Product Hunt's third place went to /dev/null, with 526 votes. The largest quake, M5.0, struck 114 km west of Petrolia, California.

A snapshot taken in one minute settles the usual argument about which feed moved first. Everything is measured against the same clock, so when five sources lean the same way, that is shared attention and not a delay in reporting. Tomorrow's edition will show how long the interest lasts, which a single day cannot.
